name: Dynamic Programming (1D/2D state)
description: Break a problem into overlapping subproblems where the optimal solution can be built from optimal solutions to smaller subproblems, cached to avoid recomputation.
core_technique: Identify the state (what varies between subproblems), write a recurrence relating state[i] to smaller states, then either memoize top-down (recursion + cache) or build bottom-up (iterative table).
common_pitfalls: Not identifying the correct state dimensions (e.g., missing that you need dp[i][j] not just dp[i]); off-by-one on base cases; using O(n^2) space when the recurrence only depends on the previous row/state, missing a space-optimization opportunity.

example_problems.title: Longest Common Subsequence
example_problems.why_it_fits: Classic 2D DP -- state is (i, j) position in each string, recurrence compares characters and takes the best of three transitions.

example_problems.title: House Robber
example_problems.why_it_fits: 1D DP -- state is 'max money up to house i', recurrence is max(rob this + dp[i-2], skip this = dp[i-1]).

example_problems.title: Coin Change (minimum coins)
example_problems.why_it_fits: 1D DP over amount -- state is 'min coins to make amount x', recurrence tries every coin denomination.

additional_considerations: Always state the recurrence relation and base case explicitly before coding -- interviewers weight this reasoning heavily. After getting a working solution, mention whether space can be optimized (e.g., rolling array when only the previous row is needed) since it signals deeper understanding even if you don't implement it.
